proposals.before: Before he capped his years, the province appointed him Retainer of the Council; recommended as Filial-and-Incorrupt, he rose through Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section to Registrar of the Pacification Army.
proposals.after: Before he capped his years, the province appointed him Retainer of the Council; recommended as Flourishing Talent (xiucai), he rose through Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section to Registrar of the Pacification Army.
proposals.reason: 秀才 is Flourishing Talent / Presented Scholar candidate, not 孝廉 Filial-and-Incorrupt.

proposals.before: In Song times his grandfather Guan had served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and said: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
proposals.after: In Song times his grandfather Kai had served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and said: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
proposals.reason: 覬之 is Kai/Ji, not Guan; matches the grandfather named in the chapter.

proposals.before: In Song times his grandfather Guan had once served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and told people: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
proposals.after: In Song times his grandfather Kai had once served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and told people: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
proposals.reason: 覬之 is Kai/Ji, not Guan.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; Chu Yuan was Minister of Works and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar of the Masters of Works and Minister of Works, entrusting him with bureau affairs.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; Chu Yuan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar to the Minister of Works and Minister of Education, entrusting him with bureau affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works (司空); 司空司徒主簿 are registrars under those excellencies.

proposals.before: When Yuan died, Minister of Works Wang Jian, because Yuan had utmost conduct, wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."
proposals.after: When Yuan died, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Jian, because Yuan had utmost conduct, wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."
proposals.reason: 尚書令王儉 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works.

proposals.before: Birth and entering death, death and leaving life—reason treats them like day and night.
proposals.after: Birth and entering death—reason treats them like day and night.
proposals.reason: Chinese only has 出生入死; English invents "death and leaving life."

proposals.before: His grandfather Bianzhi was Song General Who Pacifies the Army and inspector of Xiangzhou.
proposals.after: His grandfather Bianzhi was Song Garrison General (General Who Guards the Army) and inspector of Xiangzhou.
proposals.reason: 鎮軍將軍 is Zhenjun / Garrison General, not "Pacifies the Army" (that rendering fits 安軍/平軍-type titles).

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then Cadet of the Heir Apparent (zhongshe ren) and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.
proposals.reason: 太子中舍人 is not Junior Mentor (太子中庶子); the chapter uses 中舍人.

decisions.reason: s0020 has 舉秀才, the recommendation category Flourishing Talent (xiucai); Filial-and-Incorrupt would require 孝廉, which is absent.

decisions.after: In Song times his grandfather Ji had served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and said: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
decisions.reason: 其祖覬之 names the grandfather 覬之; Guan is unsupported. Mandarin reading of 覬 is Ji, so Kai is still wrong; replace Guan with Ji.

decisions.after: In Song times his grandfather Ji had once served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and told people: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
decisions.reason: Literal likewise misreads 覬之 as Guan; the personal name is Ji, not Kai or Guan.
褚淵爲尚書令 makes Chu Yuan Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not 司空; 頻以爲司空司徒主簿 makes Jizhi registrar under the Minister of Works and Minister of Education.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 褚淵爲尚書令……頻以爲司空司徒主簿

decisions.reason: 尚書令王儉 titles Wang Jian Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Minister of Works (司空) is not in this unit.
夫出生入死，理均晝夜 has only the idiom 出生入死; the parallel "death and leaving life" is invented English.

鎮軍將軍 is present and already rendered as the conventional title General Who Pacifies the Army; swapping to Garrison General / Guards the Army is terminological preference, not a factual mistranslation of office or person.

decisions.after: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then Cadet of the Heir Apparent and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.
decisions.reason: 復爲太子中舍人 is Cadet of the Heir Apparent, not Junior Mentor (太子中庶子); drop the awkward parenthetical romanization while keeping the corrected office.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0002 restores 覬之 as Ji; the personal-name claim's English and pinyin must read Gu Ji while zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence stay fixed.
The given-name claim must match the same 覬之 reading Ji advanced by r0002; Kai is not the Mandarin value of 覬.
